newsitem.title: GERMANY: BSE case may not have been German-born, Bonn says.
newsitem.headline: BSE case may not have been German-born, Bonn says.

text.p: An animal at the centre of a German scare over mad cow disease may have been imported from Britain and not born in Germany as was first thought, an Agriculture Ministry spokesman said on Friday.
The case had caused alarm in Germany, as it appeared the animal was the first one born in Germany to die of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) or mad cow disease.
But the spokesman said there were now several indications to suggest the Galloway calf, from a farm near the western town of Hoexter, had been imported, possibly from Britain.

He cited discrepancies in the animal's ear-tag and that of the cow previously assumed to have been its mother. He also said many documents relating to the calf from a farm in eastern Germany, where it was previously kept, were missing.
He said investigators were probing the possibility that Galloway cattle had been illegally imported from Britain into eastern Germany via the Czech Republic.
The case prompted swift action from German officials on Wednesday, who decided to slaughter 5,200 British and Swiss cattle. Britain and Switzerland have recorded the largest number of BSE cases.

The officials also decided to place the 14,000 offspring of the British and Swiss animals under observation until tests establish if the Galloway was born in Germany to a British mother, as was first thought.

Germany's agriculture workers' union called for stricter adherence to the ear-tag system, which indicates animals' origins, and demanded urgent measures to make sure reliable records are kept of their movements.
